items.problem: `correctness`: `ReportUser` with `ref` `a\u0000b` passes every check, because `ref` has only a byte limit (`max_len_key`, `utf8_bytes(ref)`) and neither `validation.is_plain_text` nor any other check rejects U+0000. Run through `core/ReportUser` on both DBs: SQLite returns success and writes the row; PostgreSQL returns `INTERNAL` (code 8), leaves the `error` log `unhandled exception` and writes no row. So a client gets `INTERNAL` and an `error` log for each such request, in place of `INVALID_REQUEST`, and the two DBs give different results for the same input (`storage` `## behavior` requires the same result in both DBs). Existed before the range

`efficiency`: `BlockUser` of a new target calls `public-profile.is_active_user` once per existing block row, and each call is one `storage.get_user_record` query (server/core/public-profile/index.ts:181). Measured `is_active_user` calls for six successive `BlockUser` requests: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The growing amount is the user's block row count, up to `block-report.maxBlocks` (default 100; the settings schema sets no maximum). Existed before the range

`test evidence`: no test checks the `block-report.maxCommentLength` limit in `add_report`. Replacing `settings.max_comment_length` with 1000000 at this line leaves all 46 block-report tests passing. A probe confirms the current code is right: a 4 code point comment with a limit of 3 is `INVALID_INPUT` in `add_report` and `INVALID_REQUEST` in `ReportUser`. Existed before the range

`test evidence`: `## error` sets log `none` for `INVALID_INPUT` of `add_report` in `ReportUser`, and no test checks it. Passing `log_invalid` `true` at this line leaves all 46 tests passing. Existed before the range

`test evidence`: no test checks that `expires_at` of `block_report_count` is window start + `block-report.reportWindowMs`. Making it window start + 5 × `block-report.reportWindowMs` leaves all 46 tests passing. Existed before the range

`test evidence`: no test tells the request time from `clock_now`, because no block-report test uses a cheat time offset and `server-time` puts that offset only into the request time. Each of these leaves all 46 tests passing: the fixed window from `clock_now` (index.ts:329, `## behavior` sets the request time), report `created_at` from `clock_now` (index.ts:348), block row `created_at` from `clock_now` (index.ts:415). Existed before the range

`test evidence`: `## error` sets an `error` log for a second `register_block_listener` of the same function, and the test checks only the server start failure (server/core/block-report/tests/start.test.ts:9). Deleting the log call at this line leaves all 46 tests passing. Existed before the range
